- [Skip to main content](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding#wb-cont) - [Skip to "About government"](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding#wb-info) - [Switch to basic HTML version](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding?wbdisable=true) ![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/hero/2026-10-HERO.jpg?modified=20261019212122) # Riding Mountain National Park ## Help shape the future of Riding Mountain National Park and Wasagaming. [Learn more!](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/info/politiques-plans-policies) Riding Mountain is home to a staggering diversity of living things. The windswept grasslands and deep, silent forests, of secretive wolf packs, of orchids and lilies, of lakes and wetlands singing with life. Riding Mountain National Park is in Treaty 2 Territory, where we work with Anishinabe, First Nations from treaties 2, 4, and 1. We honour, acknowledge, and recognize Indigenous contributions to the park, the province, and Canada. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/visit/2026-04-RMNP-VC-Feature.jpg?modified=20260429180346)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/visi-cent) ### [Visitor Centre](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/visi-cent) Welcome to the Riding Mountain National Park Visitor Centre. Come to explore, to share, to learn and to find your fun! [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/activ/otentik-640x360.jpg?modified=20221124183650)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping) ### [Camping](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping) Camping is permitted in designated areas only with a valid national park camping permit and a national park entry pass. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/activ/randonne-hiking-es-2025-640.jpg?modified=20250502182155)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/activ4/etat-sentiers-trail-conditions) ### [Hit the trails](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/activ4/etat-sentiers-trail-conditions) Riding Mountain’s trails are the best way to connect with it all in the spring, summer, fall, and winter. ## Most requested - [Important bulletins](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/securite-safety/bulletins) - [Fire Information and Updates](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/feu-alert-fire) - [Weather](https://weather.gc.ca/en/location/index.html?coords=50.658,-99.969) - [Road conditions](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/securite-safety/routes-road) - [Subscribe to our newsletter](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/info/courriel-email) - [Managing watercraft and protecting park waters](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/moto-boat) - [Realty and Townsite services](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/info/urbain-townsite) - [Park management plan](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/info/politiques-plans-policies) - [Camping and overnight accommodations](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping) ## Visiting Riding Mountain National Park ### [Activities and experiences](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ) Things to do, trails, tours, programs, itineraries, volunteering, and at-home activities. ### [Plan your visit](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit) How to get here, local guides and outfitters, local attractions, accessibility, facilities and services, meeting and event rentals. ### [Camping and overnight accommodations](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping) Types of accommodations, equipped camping, and nearby accommodations. ### [Reservations](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) Make a reservation for campsites, accommodations, and select activities. ### [Safety and guidelines](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/securite-safety) Important bulletins, trail conditions, weather conditions, seasonal safety, park regulations. ### [Fees](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/tarifs-fees) Free admission and discounted camping fees, program fees, and more. ### [Passes and permits](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/pass) Daily visitor fees, camping and program fees, and more. Free admission for youth. ### [Visitor guidelines](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/info/reglements-regulations) Our protected areas are unique places and require unique rules to protect them. ## About ### [Stewardship and management](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/info) Jobs, partners, film permits, research permits, public consultations, plans, and policies. ### [Nature and science](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/nature) Conservation and science, animals, plants, the environment, and research. ### [Indigenous connections](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/autochtones-indigenous-cultures) Strong relationships with Indigenous partners are essential to Parks Canada's work and contribute to the process of reconciliation. How to get here

| | ### Contact Riding Mountain National Park **General inquiries:** 204-848-7275 Fax: 204-848-2596 [rmnp.info@pc.gc.ca](mailto:rmnp.info@pc.gc.ca "rmnp.info@pc.gc.ca") **For emergencies within the park:** 1-877-852-3100 Parks Canada Dispatch ### Hours of operation [Hours vary: Complete schedule](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/heures-hours) ### \#RidingNP \#PNriding - [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/RidingNP) - [Twitter](https://x.com/RidingNP) - [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLOe6XX2wBaibrS5n5zUzpiWdwI2-S5dkt) - [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/parks.canada/) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/mb/pnmr-rmnp-est-east-640x360.jpg?modified=20221203012330)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/eastgate) ### [Riding Mountain Park East Gate Registration Complex National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/eastgate) Canada’s last remaining early 1930s-style national parks entrance, the East Gate Registration Complex stands as a carefully maintained example of this form of traditional architecture. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/mb/theforks-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220835)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/forks) ### [The Forks National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/forks) Delve 6,000 years into the past at Winnipeg’s “Meeting Place” while soaking up the bustling ambience. Learn how two great rivers at the heart of the continent connected the prairies to the world. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/mb/lowerfortgarry-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220835)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/fortgarry) ### [Lower Fort Garry National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/fortgarry) Standing on the bank of the Red River for more than 180 years, Lower Fort Garry tells inspiring tales of innovation, discovery and struggle. Chat with a 19th century Red River settler and immerse yourself in the daily life of the Fort’s inhabitants. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/mb/rielhouse-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220835)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/riel) ### [Riel House National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/riel) Travel back to spring 1886, six months after the death of Louis Riel. Visit his family home and discover what life was like for the Riel family and Métis who lived along the banks of the Red River. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/mb/standrewsrectory-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220835)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/standrews) ### [St. Andrew's Rectory National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/mb/standrews) Learn about the significance of the St Andrew’s Rectory, an excellent example of mid-19th century Red River Hudson’s Bay Company architecture. Imagine the day to day lives of the Reverend and his Red River settler parishioners in the 1800s. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/sk/sk-motherwell-640.jpg?modified=20221126215444)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/sk/motherwell) ### [Motherwell Homestead National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/sk/motherwell) Hear prairie songbirds sing and smell the sweet hay as you help feed the horses. Re-connect with Canada’s homestead life and bake bread with flour ground from grain harvested from the golden fields outside.

Visitors must bring their own or fill up in Onanole. - Winter reservations will be emailed check-in instructions for self-service. - #10 washroom facility remains open. [Lake Audy Horse Corral](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping#eaudy) | ![](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping) | Camping | | Map locations [**Camping basics**](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping/bases-basics) \| **[Reservable accommodation information](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/activ/camping/hebergement-accommodation-pcrs)** Wasagaming campground The perfect camping destination for a family vacation, Wasagaming Campground is conveniently located within walking distance of Wasagaming townsite. The Wasagaming Campground is minutes from the main beach area and pier, restaurants, playground area, tennis courts, lawn bowling, Visitor Centre, walking and biking trails, canoe, kayak and bike rentals, horseback riding, 18-hole golf course, shopping and much more. In the evening, stroll a nearby trail, roast hotdogs and marshmallows at your site, or take part in one of our campfire programs held regularly throughout the summer at the communal fire circle. To avoid missing out on booking your ideal camping experience, be sure to make a camping reservation before coming to Riding Mountain National Park. **[Map](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/pdf/Wasagaming-Campground-Map_2026_Summer_EN.pdf)** **Reservations:** **[Campground Reservations](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/)** **1-877-RESERVE** **(1-877-737-3783)** * * * ### General Information ![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/activ/hiver-winter/wcg-2023.jpg) With over 400 reservable campsites, Wasagaming Campground offers a wide range of camping experiences including fully serviced sites. **[Map](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/mb/riding/WET4/pdf/Wasagaming-Campground-Map_2026_Summer_EN.pdf)** - Open from mid-May to mid-October. \* - Reservations are highly recommended during peak season. - Maximum 6 people per site. - Check-in time: 2:00 pm. - Check-out time: 11:00 am. - Firewood – sold per bundle. #### Service Types - Unserviced - Electrical (pull-through and back-in) - Electricity and Water (back-in) - Electricity, Water and Sewer (pull-through) - Accessible sites for those with mobility impairments available in electricity/water/sewer service, electric service and water/electric service. See **Accessible Camping** for more information on how to reserve. **\\* Please note:** Only certain sections of the campground are open May-June and September-October. There will be limited water and facility services available from September to June. Please call the park directly for up-to-date information. #### Amenities - Potable water & washrooms with hot showers. - Kitchen shelters & dumping station. - Laundry, groceries and restaurants nearby. - Walking and cycling trails. - All sites have a firepit and picnic table. - Campfire programs. [Fees](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/mb/riding/visit/tarifs-fees) Accessible camping The perfect camping destination for a family vacation, Wasagaming Campground is conveniently located within walking distance of the Wasagaming townsite. Wasagaming Campground offers a selection of full-service, electric, and water/electric accessible campsites. Accessible campsites are intended for those that require them – to ensure integrity, we manage the reservations for these campsites in-house rather than through the Parks Canada Reservation System. #### Accessible Campsite Summary | Campsites | Operating Dates | Site amenities | | --- | --- | --- | | #36, #37, #38, #39, #51, #52

When you call, your information will be collected, and you will be **called back at a later date to process your reservation request.** You will be called back in the order our calls are received. Please note, sites are in high-demand and we cannot guarantee that you will get the site dates/ allocation that you prefer. **After launch day:** Please call 204-868-8267 to reserve an accessible campsite. **What should I have ready when I call to reserve?** Please have the following information ready: - Your top three preferred date ranges - Your preferred service area (full-service, electric, or water/electric) - Your preferred campsite if known - Your phone number and email address - A preferred time that we can call you back the following week **What if I wasn’t able to reserve an accessible campsite?** You will still have the chance to reserve a campsite through the Parks Canada Reservation System. Please see our frontcountry camping opportunities for all available options. Frontcountry camping - All front country camping locations include a picnic table and firepits. Most locations also have bear-proof lockers for safe food storage in addition to kitchen shelters in case the weather isn’t cooperating. - You are in bear country. The “bare campsite” policy is in place at all times (day and night) while camping or picnicking at all of our campgrounds or day-use areas. This means food, garbage, coolers and all types of scented items must be secured in a vehicle or bear box when not in use. - To maintain the family-friendly atmosphere that attracts thousands here every year, quiet hours are in place between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. During quiet hours there is also a liquor and cannabis curfew at all campgrounds. Please report noise disturbances through Parks Canada Dispatch 1-877-852-3100. - Campfires and bright lights must be out by 1:00 a.m. [Reserve your campsite now](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) #### Campground Summary | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Campground | Open | Reservable | \# of sites | Site types | | Wasagaming campground | Mid May to mid October | Reservable | 446 | - Water

Summer and fall you can stroll, run, pedal or trot nearly 370 km’s of trails in all areas of the Park, each with their own flavour. Cross country skiing, snowshoeing or fat biking along one of the nearly 130 km of winter trails is the best way that you can embrace Riding Mountain National Park in the winter season too. This magical time of the year won’t let you down and will warm your heart. - Park visitors are responsible for their own safety and must be self-sufficient in dealing with any emergency that may occur. Cell phone service is unreliable in the backcountry of RMNP - Plan your travel route - Know the terrain and conditions - Check the weather - Let someone know when and where you are going and when you expect to return. - Bring the essentials.
